title: Pascal's memorial
hookLine: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not of the philosophers: joy, tears of joy
tomorrow: a traveler sinks in a bog called Despond. who pulls him out?

lines: ONE NIGHT, ON A SCRAP OF PAPER.
cards: Crying at a graduation. Crying when the dog you thought was lost trots back up the driveway. Happy tears are strange: the body doesn't seem to know which feeling it's having.

Blaise Pascal, a French mathematician, had a night like that, and wrote it down on a scrap of paper. The story goes that after he died, it was found sewn into the lining of his coat. So that's what he kept there.

teach.b: It's called his memorial, and it isn't an essay. It's a list, almost gasped. The paper gives the date and even the hours, late at night.
Then one word in capitals: FEU, fire. Then: "Dieu d'Abraham, Dieu d'Isaac, Dieu de Jacob, non des philosophes et des savants."
God of Abraham, of Isaac, of Jacob, not of the philosophers and scholars.
Those first names come from the burning bush, where God says to Moses: "I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob."
A God with family names, met, not argued into. Then certainty, peace, and the line people remember: "Joie, joie, joie, pleurs de joie."
Joy, joy, joy, tears of joy.
Here's the thing to tell a friend: a man of proofs kept this one thing close, and it has no proof in it at all.

how: Pascal's memorial is printed with his Pensées and read by Christians of many churches; some people keep a short written record of moments when God seemed near.

s: Pascal's memorial is a long essay proving God exists
it's a short list, almost gasped: fire, the God of Abraham, certainty, peace, joy, tears of joy.
the memorial's names for God come from the burning bush in Exodus
I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
'not of the philosophers' means Pascal thought thinking was worthless
the memorial says nothing like that. it sets a God met by name beside a God argued about.

games.q: you find your grandfather's old notebook. one page has just a date and 'thank you, thank you.' your sister calls it cringe. what would Pascal's memorial say?
o: some moments are kept in a few words, close by, for life.
a real experience of God should be written up as a full argument.
private notes like that are better thrown away.
games.why: Pascal's whole memorial is a few gasped words and a date, and the story goes he kept it sewn in his coat.

practice: With a pen, by hand, write down one moment of joy from this week, in as few words as Pascal used: a name, a place, one word.
Fold the paper and keep it somewhere close, a pocket, a wallet, a phone case, and sit quietly with it there.

wordCard.voice: Pascal's memorial. One night of fire, written on a scrap, and kept close: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and tears of joy.

orig.note: Hebrew: God of Abraham, from Exodus 3:6, the name Pascal's memorial calls on.

carryVoice: Your line: joy, joy, tears of joy. Seven lines in seven days, and the newest one came with tears. A week, done.
